newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Ben & Jerry's sees Benelux break-even in 1998.
newsitem.headline: Ben & Jerry's sees Benelux break-even in 1998.

text.p: Ben & Jerry's Homemade Inc., which began selling its ice cream in Belgium Monday, said it was aiming for a break-even in the three-country Benelux region next year.
"We expect to operate at break-even by 1998," said Rens Groeneveld, head of operations of Ben & Jerry's Benelux.
The company, which aims to blend the sale of ice cream with the promotion of social improvement, was introduced in the Netherlands last year and is currently available there at about 450 outlets.
Depending on the level of succes in Belgium, the brand could be launched in Luxembourg in a year.
In Belgium, Ben & Jerry's will initially sell eight of its palette of 50 flavors at selected supermarkets and snack shops at 190 francs ($5.33) per half litre (quart) container.
Groeneveld, who described the Belgian market as "the den of the ice cream tastebuds," said Ben & Jerry's had no immediate plans for a major advertising campaign.

Ben & Jerry's, whose ice cream is imported directly from the company's Vermont headquarters and is also available in France and Britain, donates 7.5 percent of pre-tax earnings to socially-oriented projects.
